acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Tools timeline list filtering, UTF-16 label projection, empty/disabled state and current UI-key-to-opaque-ID resolution move into Rust ToolsForm. Chromium retains Unicode normalization, source stores, visibility/context checks and snapshot/reopen/restore authority.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: Rust ToolsForm projects both snapshot and closed-tab choices from opaque IDs, UTF-16 title/detail and native-normalized search text. It owns matching, title/em-dash/detail labels, empty copy, enabled state and the current target maps. The opt-in path no longer allocates native SimpleComboboxModel items or populates the parallel C++ snapshot_ids_/closed_ids_ vectors.

Query normalization and source search normalization remain in the native ICU adapter. Rust matches raw UTF-16 units exactly like native find(), including partial surrogates and matches across the original title/space/detail boundary. It does not search the rendered em dash, trim input or introduce another Unicode folding policy. Display metadata may include formatted URLs; no browser URL object or authority crosses the ABI.

Each projection mints group/epoch/index UI keys, independent of display labels and opaque native IDs. Duplicate labels and IDs have distinct control keys. Refresh/reorder, query edits, form reset and page changes invalidate old targets; snapshot and closed groups cannot borrow each others keys. Counter exhaustion fails closed without reusing keys. Empty native IDs never authorize an action.

SceneSelect receives projected labels/keys and keeps its existing Rust input/prefix/menu/token state and Metal/native metric/event/focus/AX adapters. The original reset-to-first selection policy and native empty disabled placeholder behavior remain. A timeline button captures the selected projection key before posting its command. Rust resolves that captured key at admission, so a later filter cannot lend a new index-zero target to an older click. Direct current actions also resolve keys in Rust, replacing index-to-C++-vector dispatch in the opt-in path.

Native widget visibility, posted tools/workspace/profile generation checks, IME admission, active profile/workspace store lookup, beforeunload, real snapshot/session validation, persistence and rollback remain authoritative. A resolved opaque ID still requires the native service to accept the operation. Views retains its original vectors, filter, labels and native combobox model.

Four Rust cases cover raw UTF-16/surrogates/native search join, stale/reordered/reset/page/cross-group keys, independent lists/duplicate and empty IDs, and epoch exhaustion. A new shared browser case compares both live lists against the original native ICU/filter/label/AX oracle for Greek, dotted I, emoji, partial surrogate, empty and no-match queries, then uses actual Cocoa Space after successful presentation to reopen a real closed tab and restore a real snapshot. A dedicated Metal browser case changes the filter while a delete is queued, requires both old/new targets to survive, then verifies a fresh delete succeeds.

The existing duplicate-title deletion/identity, empty/disabled/hidden picker, tools editor/choice/action, Time Machine persistence/sleep/restore and stale native generation cases remain covered. No dependency or browser-store/security policy was added. Other tool form construction, service wording, native node/container ownership and full manual/performance/release acceptance remain open.

first_focused_probe.reason: The new oracle helper used empty InsertText to clear a selected query, which is a no-op in both input adapters. It now deletes the selected range. Integration review also added captured projection keys to posted actions and a dedicated stale-filter action test before final validation.

compile_probe.reason: The new C++ test needed the ICU case-conversion header and separate source lines for ASSERT_NO_FATAL_FAILURE macros. No GUI test was launched on the compile probe.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.

limits: Native titles/frames and modal/scroll/window/event/focus/AX containers, other forms/panels/layouts and remaining form construction/service wording remain open. Native browser validation, authority, stores and operations remain explicit adapters.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, global RTL, typography/scale/pixel fidelity, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup or memory improvement is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
